message.content: {"4": {"original": "\"To promote the Progress of Science and useful Arts, by securing for limited...\"", "rephrased": "The full, unedited text of the US Constitution's copyright clause reveals that the original intent was to promote the progress of science and useful arts by securing exclusive rights to authors and inventors for limited times, rather than to grant perpetual monopolies as a shortened, expurgated version might suggest. This complete wording underscores that the legal framework for copyright is fundamentally designed to advance public knowledge through temporary incentives, not to restrict access indefinitely.", "summary": "The original US Constitution copyright clause prioritizes public progress over perpetual author monopolies."}}
